title: Canceled worker delegation keeps a handle on its isolated worktree directory: git worktree remove leaves an empty dir with Permission denied (Windows)
outcome: After a worker delegation is canceled and its child session has ended, nothing in TermAl (host or child runtime) keeps a handle on the child's isolated worktree directory, so a non-forced `git worktree remove` removes the directory completely.
acceptance: Root cause identified with file:line: which process or handle (child runtime cwd, host watcher, app-server thread cwd, or open file) still holds the canceled child's worktree directory, and when it would release.

Fix plus behavioral test on Windows: cancel a worker delegation with an isolated worktree, then a non-forced worktree removal of that directory succeeds, leaving no empty directory, without force and without killing processes.
The review pair is clean and the full gate passes on the exact landed input, including the Windows leg.
